column1: So we start off with a linear operator from V to V, and can we find a good basis so that the matrix of T is in simple form? So let's think about that a little bit. First of all, you have a notion—when you have a linear operator on a vector space, you have a notion of an invariant subspace.

column1: If you have an invariant subspace, it is a subspace of V which is preserved under T, such that T(W) is contained in W.
column2: 所谓不变子空间，是 V 的一个子空间，它在 T 的作用下保持不变，即 T(W) 包含于 W 中。

column1: So if you apply T to any vector in W, you stay in W: that's what it means: invariant under T.
column2: 也就是说，如果你把 T 作用于 W 中的任意向量，结果仍然留在 W 中：这就是“在 T 下不变”的含义。

column1: Now if you have an invariant subspace already, and you choose your basis so that you start off with basis elements of W and then you complete them to basis elements of V, then the matrix of T has a special form.
column2: 现在如果你已经有了一个不变子空间，并且你选取基时先从 W 的基元素开始，然后将它们扩充为 V 的基元素，那么 T 的矩阵就具有一种特殊的形式。

column1: Namely, if you start off with your basis vectors in W, say the first few basis vectors in W, the coordinates when you transform them under T lie in W, so only involve the first few terms.
column2: 也就是说，如果你从 W 中的基向量出发（比如说前几个基向量落在 W 中），当你在 T 作用下变换它们时，坐标仍落在 W 中，因此只涉及前几项。

column1: So you get a little square matrix here—we'll call that matrix A, maybe—and then down here you get all zeros, because when you apply it to a vector in W, it doesn't involve any of the basis vectors that are beyond W.
column2: 所以你在这里得到一个小方阵——不妨称该矩阵为 A——而在其下方，你得到全零，因为当你把它作用于 W 中的向量时，它不涉及 W 之外的任何基向量。

column1: And then when you apply that to the other basis vectors, you don't know anything about it at all, so you might get a B here and a D here, but you get a lot of zeros in the matrix if you have an invariant subspace and you choose your basis so the first basis vectors are in W.

column1: Now even better than an invariant subspace is an invariant subspace with an invariant complement.
column2: 现在，比不变子空间更好的是具有不变补空间的不变子空间。

column1: To have an invariant complement W' means another subspace of V such that any vector in V is uniquely of the form of a vector in W plus a vector in W', and we write that V is the direct sum of W and W', V = W ⊕ W'.
column2: 拥有不变补空间 W' 意味着 V 的另一个子空间，使得 V 中的任意向量都可以唯一地表示为 W 中的向量加上 W' 中的向量的形式，我们记作 V 是 W 与 W' 的直和，V = W ⊕ W'。

column1: So you get two subspaces, and any vector is uniquely of the form of a vector in W plus a vector in W'. And T(W') is contained in W', namely it's another invariant subspace.
column2: 于是你得到两个子空间，且任意向量都唯一表示为 W 中向量与 W' 中向量之和。并且 T(W')包含在 W' 中，也就是说它也是一个不变子空间。

column1: Then the matrix looks even simpler: the matrix A of the transformation, if we choose a basis of W and adjoin it to a basis of W' to get a full basis of V, then our matrix A looks like this: a square matrix on W, a square matrix on W', and zeros elsewhere.
